inputs.original_text: This proposed legislation in New York's 2026 State of the State agenda would require guns sold in the state to be built so they can't be easily modified into illegal machine guns, along with criminal penalties for violations. It's a vital push to confront the structural inequalities that allow the gun industry to fuel violence in our most vulnerable communities. For too long, corporations have exploited weak standards rooted in historical power imbalances, leaving marginalized groups and working people to bear the deadly costs. These reforms are essential to put safety and accountability first over corporate interests, protecting those hit hardest by systemic failures in public safety.
inputs.modified_text: Yet another overreach from the New York politicians in their 2026 State of the State agenda. They're proposing rules that would force guns sold in the state to be built so they can't be easily modified into illegal machine guns, along with criminal penalties for violations. This is being dressed up as some effort against structural inequalities and corporate power, but it's really just another progressive attack on our constitutional traditions of self-reliance and the right to defend our families. Instead of promoting personal responsibility, strong law enforcement, and cultural order, these reforms put more restrictions on law-abiding citizens while ignoring the real drivers of disorder like family breakdown and failed urban policies. We need to reject this kind of government meddling that weakens national strength in the name of protecting the vulnerable.
